description:
Staff is requesting approval of a Master Services Agreement with ARAG Insurance Company and ARAG Services, LLC for the provision of a voluntary, employee-paid legal services plan. The plan, branded as ARAG UltimateAdvisor Plus, would be offered to all City employees as a supplemental benefit available through payroll deduction.
Prepaid legal plans provide employees with affordable access to attorney services for common personal legal matters such as estate planning (wills, trusts, and powers of attorney), real estate transactions, family law consultations, traffic violations, identity theft defense, and document review. The ARAG UltimateAdvisor Plus plan provides access to a nationwide network of attorneys at no out-of-pocket cost to the employee for covered services. The monthly premium is $21.96 per employee ($263.52 annually), paid entirely by the enrolled employee through after-tax payroll deduction. There is no cost to the City.
Eligible employees may enroll within thirty (30) days of beginning employment, upon a qualifying life status change, or during the annual open enrollment period. Enrolled employees are required to remain in the plan for the duration of the plan year.
The agreement has an initial term beginning October 1, 2026 and ending September 30, 2029, providing a three-year rate guarantee at the $21.96 monthly rate. After the initial term, the agreement terminates unless ARAG provides and the City accepts a contract renewal. Either party may terminate the agreement due to a material breach upon thirty (30) days' written notice. The agreement has been reviewed and redlined by the City Attorney, and all statutorily required contract provisions under Florida law are incorporated by reference.
title: Consideration re: Master Services Agreement with ARAG Insurance Company/ARAG Services, LLC for Voluntary Employee-Paid Prepaid Legal Services Plan

description:
A Right-of-Way Construction Permit is required for any construction, installation, or modification of improvements within a municipality’s public right-of-way. The City of DeLand is experiencing sustained population growth and commercial development, leading to a significant increase in construction and utility activities within city rights-of-way. Our roadways, roadside margins, sidewalks, multi-use paths, utility corridors, drainage swales, and public fixtures represent the city’s most substantial and critical capital investments.Historically, right-of-way construction activity in DeLand has been managed through a manual, email-based review process at no cost to applicants. While this informal approach met previous demands, the growing volume and complexity of utility installations, underground excavations, and private development now necessitate a modernized oversight framework.
Right-of-Way Construction permitting requires contractors to coordinate with Sunshine 811, utility agencies/owners, and the city to prevent damage to critical underground infrastructure. The associated engineering reviews enforce city construction standards, protecting our road bases, intersection sightlines, and stormwater management systems. The permitting process also enhances public safety by requiring approved traffic control plans for work zones and by notifying emergency services of any lane closures in advance to prevent delays in their response time.
Right-of-Way Use permitting requires developers to obtain formal authorization from the City of DeLand before connecting any County- or State-approved development to a City-owned and maintained roadway. This permitting process safeguards public safety, ensures access design complies with City engineering standards, and preserves the operational capacity and traffic flow of the corridor.
An effective right-of-way permitting system serves not only as an administrative formality, but as a vital risk management and quality control tool that safeguards taxpayer-funded infrastructure, maintains city aesthetics, and protects the community.
title: Second Reading of Ordinance 2026-19, Establishing a Formal Right-of-Way Permitting Process, Adopting the Associated Right-of-Way Construction Permit Fee Schedule and Requirements, and Approving the Right-of-Way Construction Permit Supplemental Conditions.

description: An Ordinance is proposed to the City Commission to amend Section 30-20 of Chapter 30 of the Code of Ordinances relating to water and wastewater development/connection fees. The Ordinance implements the recommendations of the 2026 GovRates, Inc. connection fee study, which reflect higher capital costs driven by inflation and are intended to ensure that growth continues to pay its own way. Unlike the prior amendment, which increased only the wastewater connection charges, this Ordinance increases both the water and the wastewater development connection fees. The water development connection fee will increase from $2,580.00 to $6,375.00 per equivalent residential unit (ERU), based on a unit rate of $318.75 per fixture unit. The wastewater development connection fee will increase from $5,257.00 to $7,320.00 per ERU, based on a unit rate of $366.00 per fixture unit. All residential units will be charged a connection fee equal to one ERU. The Ordinance also makes conforming updates to the fee-computation methodology and technical revisions to the text of the current provisions. The revised fees take effect October 1, 2026.
title: Second Reading of Ordinance 2026-22: Amending Chapter 30 of the Code of Ordinances, Section 30-20 Relating to Development/Connection Fees

description:
Approximately 43 residents currently live at the DeLand Municipal Mobile Home Park. The current residents pay $325 per month for rent, regardless of the trailer size. The rent figure includes lot rental, property tax, lawn maintenance, water, sewer, garbage and stormwater. The City increased the monthly rental rates by $25 effective January 1, each of the last seven years. Before that, the municipal mobile home park had not seen a rental increase since 2009. Similar parks in Volusia County range from an average of $567 per month for all age parks (so-called "family parks") to $827 per month for 55+ parks for lot rental alone. Due to this fact, staff recommends increasing the rental rate by another $30 per month. The proposed new lot rental rate would be $355 per month, regardless of the trailer size.
The lot rental increase requires a 90-day notice to the homeowners before it can take effect. Therefore, with approval from the City Commission, staff will send out notices during the month of September 2026 in order for the lot rental increases to take effect January 1, 2027.
title: Consideration re: Rental Increases for DeLand Municipal Mobile Home Park.

description:
Stetson University is requesting approval to remove one (1) historic tree located at 359 East Michigan Avenue, Stetson University, Nemec Hall dormitory parking lot. The Land Development Regulations require that, before the removal of any historic trees should occur, it shall be approved by the City Commission. Section 33-57.05(d) states that there must be a finding that the tree is a hazard (due to health or natural damage) or that it is not economically or practically feasible to develop the parcel without removing the tree. The City Forester has determined that the tree proposed for removal is a dead 40” DBH historic Live Oak tree. The applicant, Stetson University, is requesting the removal because the tree is a hazard due to its dead condition.
At the September 8th Tree Advisory Committee meeting, the Arborist Inspector’s PowerPoint was presented demonstrating the tree proposed for removal is a 40” DBH historic Live Oak tree that is dead. The applicant is requesting the removal of the tree because the tree is a hazard due to its condition. Because of the tree’s deteriorated and dead condition, by a unanimous vote, the Tree Advisory Committee recommended approval of the removal of the 40” Live Oak tree with a replacement requirement of one (1) six- (6-) inch caliper Live Oak tree to be planted on the Stetson University campus. It was the opinion of the Tree Advisory Committee members voting to approve the removal that reduced replacement would be appropriate to help restore the lost canopy without unnecessarily burdening the Stetson University by requiring 100 percent DBH replacement.
title: Consideration re: Resolution 2026-52, Authorizing Removal of One (1) Historic Tree Located at 359 East Michigan Avenue, Stetson University, Nemec Hall Dormitory Parking Lot

description:
The Volunteer of the Year Award has been given annually since at least 2018 to a greater DeLand-area volunteer, who goes above and beyond the call of duty. The nominee must have been engaged in volunteer activities for a minimum of one year in the greater DeLand area. The city also created a separate recognition for "Under 40 Volunteers of the Year." A committee of community members is convened to approve the application, review all submitted applications, and make the selection of the Volunteers of the Year. Honorees have their names memorialized in a spot in Downtown DeLand.
The City Clerk's Office has facilitated this process in recent years and recently began reaching out to previous committee members to gauge their interest in serving again. In that process, discussion arose at the staff level about potential changes to the program, specifically changing the recognition from an annual occurrence to once every five (5) or ten (10) years. This change would allow for a greater applicant pool and ensure that the recognition is going to individuals invested in the community. We are requesting discussion and direction from the Commission to determine if there is interest in implementing this change. If so, we would next honor an individual in 2030 and subsequently in 2035 and/or 2040. Should the Commission wish to keep the annual recognition in place, we will proceed with identifying remaining committee members and continue as normal with a recognition planned for early 2027.
title: Discussion re: Volunteer of the Year Award

description:
The City Commission adopted Resolution No. 2015-15 establishing guidelines for ad valorem tax abatement for qualified new or expanding businesses. Per Florida Statutes, the exemption does not apply to taxes levied for the payment of bonds. September 1st is the date established in the resolution for companies entitled to tax abatement to report the number of employees and wage scale. The City Commission adopted Ordinance No. 2018-11 granting, under certain conditions, ad valorem tax exemption to Total Renal Laboratories, Inc. Each year, an "Ad Valorem Tax Exemption certificate" is required from the company certifying the number of employees and average wage on January 24th. Based on that data and the guidelines approved by the City Commission, a report is made to the City Commission on the company if it qualifies for economic tax exemption and the amount of exemption they are entitled to.
Based on the current year's data provided, Total Renal Laboratories, Inc. qualifies for a 100% tax exemption this year.
It should be noted this is the ninth tax year for Total Renal Laboratories, Inc. to be eligible for tax abatement. Ordinance No. 2018-11 granted a ten year economic development ad valorem tax exemption to Total Renal Laboratories, Inc. beginning with the 2018 tax year, up to and including the tax year of 2027.
title: Consideration re: 2026 Tax Abatement for Total Renal Laboratories, Inc.

description:

Property & Crime
The premium for Property and Crime coverage decreased by .17% even with a 32% increase in additional property value. The premium amount quoted is $1,032,021.00.
Boiler & Machinery
The premium for Boiler & Machinery coverage decreased by 12%. The premium quoted is $26,284.00.
Liability
The liability market has been fairly stable except for Law Enforcement & Auto. For Auto Liability, vehicle repairs have seen an overall increase due to the unavailability of parts. Distracted driving has also driven up claims in the pool. Liability increased 5% due to claims history and increased payroll. The premium quoted is $313,855.00. The rate remained flat.
Workers' Compensation
The workers' compensation premium showed a 5% increase due to claims history and an increase in payroll. The premium amount quoted is $263,400.00. The rate remained flat.
Excess Crime
The excess crime premium showed a .18% increase. The premium amount quoted is $5,377.00.
Ex-Wind Property
The ex-wind property rate increased by 16% due to an increase in property value. The premium amount quoted is $67,615.00.
Pollution
Pollution liability premium showed a 5% decrease. The premium amount is $29,283.00.
Cyber Liability
The cyber liability coverage remains the same from the previous year.
Airport
Airport liability coverage remains the same from the previous year. The premium quoted is $4,917.00.
** Premiums are subject to change based on increases/decreases to payroll, property exposure and claim history**

description:
The City of DeLand requires CT Calcium Score imaging services for use in pre-employment screening of prospective firefighter candidates and as a component of the annual firefighter physical evaluations to ensure all firefighters meet the applicable fitness-for-duty requirements. The City's previous provider of these services unexpectedly became unable to continue performing the scans, creating an immediate need for a replacement provider.
Staff identified SimonMed Imaging (SMI Imaging, LLC), a nationally recognized diagnostic imaging provider, as a qualified replacement. SimonMed has agreed to provide CT Calcium Score services at a rate of $80.00 per scan, which is the same rate the City paid under its previous contract.
The proposed Preferred Provider Agreement has an initial term of one (1) year commencing on the Effective Date, with automatic renewal for successive one-year periods. Either party may terminate the agreement with or without cause upon ninety (90) days' written notice. SimonMed will bill the City directly and will not seek any remuneration from individual patients.
Any examinations ordered outside of the CT Calcium Score service outlined in Exhibit A of the agreement will be billed at 100% of SimonMed's usual and customary fee schedule.
title: Consideration re: Preferred Provider Agreement with SMI Imaging, LLC (SimonMed Imaging) for CT Calcium Score Diagnostic Imaging Services for Firefighter Pre-Employment and Annual Fitness-for-Duty Evaluations

description:

The next and final phase of data collection has been budgeted by the Public Works Department for $25,000. The Public Works Department has received a quote from PlanIt GEO in the amount of $16,000. Public Works staff are familiar with the software and believe that trying to export the data into another vendors program would result in corrupted or lost data. This is a sole source request in the amount of $16,000 to allow PlanIT GEO to continue with the City’s tree inventory data collection which would bring this project to completion.

description:
Florida Chapter 2026-63 which was enacted on July 1, 2026 requires that a building permit issued for a single-family dwelling expires 1 year after the issuance of the permit or on the effective date of the next edition of the Florida Building Code, whichever is later (see below).
(c) A local government that issues building permits may send a written notice of expiration, by e-mail or United States Postal Service, to the owner of the property and the contractor listed on the permit, no less than 30 days before a building permit is set to expire. The written notice must identify the permit that is set to expire and the date the permit will expire. A building permit issued by a local government for a single-family dwelling expires 1 year after the issuance of the permit or on the effective date of the next edition of the Florida Building Code, whichever is later. However, this paragraph does not prevent a local government from extending a building permit beyond the expiration date.
Chapter 7, Section 7-2, paragraph 105.5 is being amended to comply with this requirement.
In addition, Chapter 7, Section 7-1 (c) is being removed as this standard is now located in the Build Permit Fee Schedule which was approved by the City Commission on August 17, 2026.
On August 17, 2026, the City Commission approved the ordinance on First Reading.
title: Second Reading of Ordinance 2026-20, Amending Chapter 7 - Building and Housing Codes of the Code Of Ordinances

description: An Ordinance is proposed to the City Commission to amend Section 30-20 of Chapter 30 of the Code of Ordinances relating to water and wastewater development/connection fees. The Ordinance implements the recommendations of the 2026 GovRates, Inc. connection fee study, which reflect higher capital costs driven by inflation and are intended to ensure that growth continues to pay its own way. Unlike the prior amendment, which increased only the wastewater connection charges, this Ordinance increases both the water and the wastewater development connection fees. The water development connection fee will increase from $2,580.00 to $6,375.00 per equivalent residential unit (ERU), based on a unit rate of $318.75 per fixture unit. The wastewater development connection fee will increase from $5,257.00 to $7,320.00 per ERU, based on a unit rate of $366.00 per fixture unit. All residential units will be charged a connection fee equal to one ERU. The Ordinance also makes conforming updates to the fee-computation methodology and technical revisions to the text of the current provisions. The revised fees take effect October 1, 2026.

description:
Florida Chapter 2026-63 which was enacted on July 1, 2026 requires that a building permit issued for a single-family dwelling expires 1 year after the issuance of the permit or on the effective date of the next edition of the Florida Building Code, whichever is later (see below).
(c) A local government that issues building permits may send a written notice of expiration, by e-mail or United States Postal Service, to the owner of the property and the contractor listed on the permit, no less than 30 days before a building permit is set to expire. The written notice must identify the permit that is set to expire and the date the permit will expire. A building permit issued by a local government for a single-family dwelling expires 1 year after the issuance of the permit or on the effective date of the next edition of the Florida Building Code, whichever is later. However, this paragraph does not prevent a local government from extending a building permit beyond the expiration date.
Chapter 7, Section 7-2, paragraph 105.5 is being amended to comply with this requirement.
In addition, Chapter 7, Section 7-1 (c) is being removed as this standard is now located in the Build Permit Fee Schedule which is being considered in a separate item in this meeting's agenda.

description:
Ray Bahrami, Engineering Director, on behalf of the City of DeLand Engineering Division, has requested permission to remove one historic tree located within the City’s Boston Avenue right-of-way as part of a proposed capital improvements project to construct a sidewalk. The Land Development Regulations require that, before the removal of any historic tree should occur, it must be approved by the City Commission. Section 33-57.05(d) states that there must be a finding that the tree is a hazard (due to health or natural damage) or that it is not economically or practically feasible to develop the parcel without removing the tree.
The City Forester has determined that the tree proposed for removal is a 25” DBH historic Live Oak in fair condition. The applicant would like to remove the tree for a sidewalk improvement project along the Boston Avenue right-of-way.
At their May 12, 2026 meeting, the Tree Advisory Committee (TAC) recommended to table the request for further discussion at the next TAC meeting requesting the City Engineer of Record attend the June TAC meeting. At their June 8, 2026 TAC meeting, with the condition the proposed sidewalk improvement project is approved for construction, the Committee unanimously voted to recommend approval of the removal of the Live Oak tree located within the Boston Avenue right-of-way.
City staff recommends the removal be approved and that the required replacement be one tree from the City’s List of Approved Tree Replacement Species with a minimum six-inch caliper.
title: Consideration re: Approval of Resolution 2026-42, Authorizing Removal of One Historic Tree Located within the Boston Avenue City Right-of-Way

description:

Two items have come up in the utilities department that will require an outside contract to perform.
A month ago, the city was advised that the 12” water main aerial canal crossing on CR92 at Lake Miller overflow to Little Haw Creek was facing a possible failure. Upon investigation, the dirt that has supported the concrete structures and pipe casing on the embankment is eroding away. The Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT) is not going to address the erosion and are requiring a major project to bring it into compliance instead. Staff looked at options and feels that doing a directional drill for approximately four hundred feet under the canal will resolve the issue and be cheaper and quicker to complete to avoid a failure. A price was requested to under take the replacement task and remove the old structure’s from FDOT right away.
The other task is for a manhole adjustment in Patterson Park. The manhole is sticking out of the ground approximately one foot and is located off the road in the grass at Patterson Avenue and Hamilton Road and needs lowered due to possibility of damage from large trucks driving over the manhole. The task will cover the dismantling of the current manhole structure down to the base unit. A new 12” load bearing flat deck will be placed over the opening and new ring and cover installed and adjusted to ground level. The manhole will then be relined and stabilized soil will be placed around the manhole to support truck traffic. This task is expected to be reimbursed back to the city by the company having the turning radius issue.

description:
The Utilities Department has been testing and working on how to come into compliance with the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) on Polyfluoroalkyl and Substances, man-made forever chemicals (PFAS) removal from the cities drinking water system. Testing has shown that six of the eleven water plants have a MCL limit that is above the recommended proposed levels. Current EPA deadline for compliance is April 2029, but a possible change to extend to 2031 has been recommended but not adopted. The City’s water system currently serves an area of almost ninety-nine square miles and about 27,000 customers with potable water. The system’s twenty wells currently pump an average of about 5.6 million gallons per day (MGD). Due to good groundwater quality, treatment is currently limited to aeration, addition of chlorine and a corrosion inhibitor. The recommended treatment is to add several large diameter resin vessels that the water would follow through and capture the PFAS elements in the drinking water prior to being placed into the distribution system.
The city hired McKim & Creed Engineer firm to assist with this project. They have put together a Water Facility Plan for the Implementation of PFAS Treatment Improvements and have helped with submitting for an application for a Drinking Water State Revolving Loan Fund (DWSRF) loan. The Facility Plan shows a concept site plan at each location that shows the vessels, piping, and lift station for concentrate disposal on backwash. The financial section shows the estimated cost to be just less than $60 million.
At present, the most favorable way to finance this project is through the State’s revolving fund (SRF) loan program. The city has borrowed money for utility projects from this program in the past. Advantages include very low interest rates, low closing costs and the possibility of “loan forgiveness”.
As part of the process for SRF application, the city must request inclusion from the Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP) bureau of facility funding. The request for inclusion must be accompanied by a Facility Plan and Business Plan. These documents, attached to this request for Commission action must be reviewed and approved by a resolution of the City Commission following a public hearing on the matter.
title: Public Hearing and Resolution to Approve State Revolving Fund Facility Plan and Business Plan for Water Plant PFAS Treatment and Removal Project

The selected site represents the optimal location to improve response times and enhance emergency service delivery to residents and visitors within this growing section of the City. In addition to improving emergency response capabilities, Fire Station 84 will provide operational relief to Fire Station 81, currently the busiest fire station in Volusia County. By redistributing call volume and emergency incidents, the new station will increase system capacity within the downtown service area, improve unit availability, and help reduce firefighter workload and fatigue. The construction of Fire Station 84 represents a strategic investment in public safety infrastructure that will enhance community protection, support firefighter wellness, and ensure the City is positioned to meet current and future emergency service demands.
We have received confirmation that our House Representative, Webster Barnaby, is willing to sponsor a Florida Legislative Appropriation, or House Appropriations Local Funding Initiative request for Fire Station 84. These funding requests typically assume part of the cost for construction, and not full cost. In order to apply for this grant in September of this year, we will need to submit a preliminary design.
The subject task assignment will provide Architectural, Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing, Fire Protection, Structural, Geotechnical, Civil and Surveying services for the schematic design (30%) phase of this project. The remainder of the design phase, permitting, and bid phase assistance will be covered under a separate proposal in the future.
title: Consideration, JL2 Architecture Design Services, Fire Station 84

attachments.name: Domestic Violence Transparency Initiative Letter of Support

description:
County Council Member, Matt Reinhart is requesting support to create the Volusia County Domestic Violence Database Transparency Initiative. The proposed initiative would increase public awareness and transparency regarding domestic violence offenses in our community.
Domestic violence remains one of the most serious public safety challenges facing Volusia County, which consistently ranks among the highest counties in Florida. In fact, Volusia County recently ranked number four for domestic violence incidents for the state. While criminal case information is publicly available, locating domestic violence-related offenses often requires individuals to search through extensive court records and criminal histories.
His proposal would create a dedicated public database containing basic information on domestic violence offenses, making already-public information easier for residents to access while fully protecting victim privacy. Victim names and identifying information would not be included.
He has received approval from the County Council to have this proposed initiative included in Florida's 2027 legislative request package. He also has support from Sheriff Mike Chitwood and the Volusia County Domestic Abuse Council. The goal if for this to be a state-wide database.
This proposal is not intended to impose additional punishment beyond the legal process. Its purpose is to provide greater transparency and empower residents with access to information that is already public but often difficult to locate.
title: Consideration re: Letter of Support for Domestic Violence Database Transparency Initiative

description:
The applicant is requesting to rezone the ±2.02-acre subject property from Springwood Town Homes PD (Planned Development), to R-16 (Multi-Family Dwelling). The property is adjacent to residential and commercial uses with the SR 15A truck route to the south and west.The future land use is High Density Residential. The overall PD, approved in 2006, included three parcels, on ± 7.35 acres of property. The intent of the PD was to provide for multi-family development with a maximum density of 16 dwelling units per acre on a ± 5.33 acre portion of the development, and a single-family dwelling on the remaining portion.
The purpose of the R-16 zoning district is to provide for high-density multifamily residential living in the older developed section of DeLand and providing a spacious, well maintained and natural environment in proximity to the City’s downtown. A school concurrency letter dated May 5, 2026, was provided, stating that the Volusia County School District has no objections to the proposed development plan. Staff will review the traffic methodology at the time of plat or site plan review. If the proposed development generates more than 1,000 average daily trips, a full traffic study will be required per the Volusia Flagler Transportation Planning Organization traffic study guidelines. Stormwater retention will be designed at the time of site plan or subdivision platting. The stormwater system shall be designed to retain the 100-year, 24-hour storm event on-site, and should be designed to incorporate LID (Low Impact Development). The R-16 zoning district allows a maximum of fifty to sixty percent impervious surfaces depending on the building height and fifteen percent of the site will need to be dedicated as Tree Protection Area.
The analysis presented in the staff report suggests the proposed rezoning meets the criteria of 33-135 and is consistent with the Comprehensive Plan, future land use, zoning and character of the surrounding area, and will not have an impact upon public health, safety and welfare.
At the May 13, 2026, Planning Board meeting, the Board voted 7-0 to recommend approval of the rezoning request.
On June 15, 2026, the City Commission approved the requested R-16 rezoning on first reading.

description:
The City of DeLand is requesting approval to remove one historic tree located at 342 Churchill Downs Boulevard, in the Saddlebrook Subdivision. The Land Development Regulations (LDR) require that, before the removal of any historic tree should occur, it must be approved by the City Commission. In accordance with Section 33-57.05(d) of the LDR there must be a finding that the tree is a hazard (due to health or natural damage) or that it is not economically or practically feasible to develop the parcel without removing the tree.
The City Forester has determined that the tree proposed tree for removal is a 26” DBH historic Live Oak tree in good condition. The tree presents multiple tripping hazards due to continuous lifting of the adjacent sidewalk and driveway apron, despite repeated efforts to grind the sidewalk panels. As it is no longer structurally possible to grind the panels further, tree roots within the critical root zone would need to be cut significantly in order to repair the sidewalk areas of safety concern. The City of DeLand is requesting that the tree is removed so that both sidewalk and driveway may be replaced to prevent further tripping hazards.
At their May 12, 2026 meeting, the Tree Advisory Committee voted in a split 3:3 on the motion made to recommend the removal of the 26” DBH Live Oak tree.
title: Approval of Resolution 2026-29: Removal of one Historic Live Oak Tree Located at 342 Churchill Downs Boulevard

description:
The request is for voluntary annexation of ± 25.44 acres of property into the City limits of DeLand. The subject property is located in unincorporated Volusia County with Volusia County zoning designations of B-6, BPUD, and A-2 and is located within the City’s emerging gateway corridor overlay zoning district. The property’s Volusia County future land uses are Commercial and Rural.
The application for annexation is accompanied by requests for a small-scale future land use map amendment (SMLU24-213) and rezoning (Z26-041). If the requests are approved, the applicant intends to submit for platting and site plan review.
Chapter 171 of the Florida Statutes sets forth procedures for adjusting municipal boundaries to ensure sound urban development, accommodation for growth, and ensure that areas are not annexed unless municipal services can be provided in those areas. These procedures require the development be reasonably compact, not circuitous, and does not create an enclave. In addition, the City’s guidelines for annexation require a property be sufficiently contiguous to property already within the city limits. The parcel is contiguous to the City’s municipal’s boundary on the north and west sides and is reasonably compact. Annexation of the property does not create an area that is enclosed and bounded on all sides by the City. Furthermore, the County and City have a long standing Utility Service Agreement that properties must annex to obtain City Utilities when contiguous with jurisdictional boundaries. Therefore, staff finds the annexation request to be consistent with Chapter 171 of the State Statutes, the City’s Comprehensive Plan, and Land Development Regulations.
At their April 15, 2026, meeting, the Planning Board voted 5-0 to recommend approval of the voluntary annexation.
On May 4, 2026, the City Commission approved the annexation on first reading.
title: Second Reading of Ordinance 2026-14: Annexing ±25.44 Acres of Property, Located South of Orange Camp Road, West of the I-4 Interchange.

description:
The applicant is requesting to amend the future land use designation for ±22.43-acres of property from Volusia County: Commercial and Volusia County: Rural land use designations to the Highway Commercial (HC) land use designation. The subject property is located within the City’s emerging gateway corridor overlay zoning district. The request for a small-scale future land use map amendment is accompanied by requests for annexation (AN24-212) and rezoning (Z26-041). If the requests are approved, the applicant intends to submit for platting and site plan review.
Per the 2050 Vision plan, the subject property is located within the Category 2, Urban Core. The Urban Core is described as the area where the majority of the new growth will take place. The Comprehensive Plan describes the Highway Commercial land use designation as being typified by office, service-oriented, and commercial uses which provide retail and related goods and services to local-sub-regional and regional markets. Areas designated as Highway Commercial tend to be located in the outlying or newly developed areas of the city. Neighborhood convenience centers shall be located within easy walking distance of residents in the area, and where they will be compatible with the character of the surrounding area. Commercial uses located adjacent to residential uses shall utilize significant buffering and landscaping to minimize negative impacts. Future development will be reviewed to meet the requirements of the LDRs. Additionally, the applicant plans to develop commercial uses to serve the surrounding area. Therefore, the request is compatible with the Comprehensive Plan and the 2050 Vision Plan.
The proposed land use designation, Highway Commercial, is consistent with the surrounding area, and is not expected to create any land use incompatibilities.
In accordance with standard practice from the Florida Department of Economic Opportunity (DEO) and other review agencies, an impact comparison analysis of the proposed amendment has been completed based upon the theoretical maximum development potential under the currently adopted future land use designation versus the proposed designation. The facility analysis presented in the staff report suggests the proposed land use amendment should not cause any of the City’s public infrastructure and services to degrade below the adopted or current operational level of service (LOS) based on the theoretical maximum impact analysis.
At the April 15, 2026, Planning Board meeting, the Board voted 5-0 to recommend approval of the request for a future land use map amendment.
On May 4, 2026, the City Commission approved the request for a future land use map amendment on first reading.
On June 3, 2026, the Volusia Growth Management Commission (VGMC) issued a certificate of consistency.
title: Second Reading of Ordinance 2026-15: Changing the Land Use for ±22.43 Acres of Property, Located South of Orange Camp Road, west of the I-4 Interchange, from Volusia County Commercial and Volusia County Rural to City of DeLand Highway Commercial (HC).

description:
In 2019, the Florida Building Code was amended to restrict the value of un-expended building permit revenue fees that are carried over from a prior year. In 2024 and 2025, the Building Permit fees were reduced to achieve statutory compliance. Currently, the average operating budget for the Building Department for the past four years is $3,442,298. The unrestricted fund balance, at the end of September 2025, was approximately $4,009,289. Owing to State, Federal and Global economic and political factors, the Building Division has experienced a significant reduction in Building Permit activity and associated revenues. At the end of April 2026, that reserve has been reduced to $2,388,655 and staff projects it will be reduced to $1,162,778 by the end of this fiscal year. Due to this revenue shortfall, Building Permit fees will need to be increased by 25% to ensure that operating costs are covered to ensure that the department’s high level of customer service is maintained into the future. Staff will continue to monitor the revenues and request further adjustments if necessary. In addition, all hiring has been frozen for vacant positions in ​the Building Division.
In addition, Inspection Fees were adjusted to reflect the true cost of this service.
title: Resolution Approving Revised Building Permit Fee Schedule.

description: The City's professional staff has for quite some time planned ahead for the Beresford Avenue extension out to State Road 44 in order to alleviate congestion on State Road 44. Toward that end, the City has been working closely with Volusia County on the acquisition of properties by both entities. The City entered into an interlocal agreement (the "Western ILA") with Volusia County regarding the construction and ongoing maintenance of the western portion of the Beresford Avenue extension from Blue Lake Avenue to the Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. Beltway. That portion is, of course, now complete. The Western ILA provided that the County would build the road and that the City would thereafter be responsible for maintenance of the road. The City and County also entered into a three-party agreement with the Volusia County School Board for the purpose of trading land through the School Board's property so that the eastern portion of the Beresford Avenue Extension could be completed from MLK to SR 44. That ILA does not address road maintenance. Through discussions between the City and County, both parties feel it makes more sense for the County to maintain the Beresford Avenue extension as it truly operates as a county road as opposed to a city road. There is a cost associated with maintenance however. As such, the city and county staffs have recommended that the County agree to maintain all of the Beresford Avenue extension and that, to create some equity for the County taking on this expense, that the City agree to maintain that portion of Minnesota Avenue from the east side of Amelia Avenue to the west side of Blue Lake Avenue, on account of the fact that road segment operates much more like a city road. City staff is requesting approval by the City Commission of the attached Interlocal Agreement which would terminate the Western ILA and address the changes referenced above.
title: Interlocal Agreement with Volusia County regarding Beresford Avenue extension.

description:
The request is for voluntary annexation of ± 25.44 acres of property into the City limits of DeLand. The subject property is located in unincorporated Volusia County with Volusia County zoning designations of B-6, BPUD, and A-2 and is located within the City’s emerging gateway corridor overlay zoning district. The property’s Volusia County future land uses are Commercial and Rural.
The application for annexation is accompanied by requests for a small-scale future land use map amendment (SMLU24-213) and rezoning (Z26-041). If the requests are approved, the applicant intends to submit for platting and site plan review.
Chapter 171 of the Florida Statutes sets forth procedures for adjusting municipal boundaries to ensure sound urban development, accommodation for growth, and ensure that areas are not annexed unless municipal services can be provided in those areas. These procedures require the development be reasonably compact, not circuitous, and does not create an enclave. In addition, the City’s guidelines for annexation require a property be sufficiently contiguous to property already within the city limits. The parcel is contiguous to the City’s municipal’s boundary on the north and west sides and is reasonably compact. Annexation of the property does not create an area that is enclosed and bounded on all sides by the City. Furthermore, the County and City have a long standing Utility Service Agreement that properties must annex to obtain City Utilities when contiguous with jurisdictional boundaries. Therefore, staff finds the annexation request to be consistent with Chapter 171 of the State Statutes, the City’s Comprehensive Plan, and Land Development Regulations.
At their April 15, 2026, meeting, the Planning Board voted 5-0 to recommend approval of the voluntary annexation.
The request for the land use amendment will be transmitted to Volusia Growth Management Commission (VGMC) for review. After VGMC review, the annexation, land use and zoning requests are anticipated to go before the City Commission on June 15, 2026 for second reading.
title: First Reading of Ordinance Annexing ±25.44 Acres of Property, Located South of Orange Camp Road, West of the I-4 Interchange.

description:
The applicant is requesting to amend the future land use designation for ±22.43-acres of property from Volusia County: Commercial and Volusia County: Rural land use designations to the Highway Commercial (HC) land use designation. The subject property is located within the City’s emerging gateway corridor overlay zoning district. The request for a small-scale future land use map amendment is accompanied by requests for annexation (AN24-212) and rezoning (Z26-041). If the requests are approved, the applicant intends to submit for platting and site plan review.
Per the 2050 Vision plan, the subject property is located within the Category 2, Urban Core. The Urban Core is described as the area where the majority of the new growth will take place. The Comprehensive Plan describes the Highway Commercial land use designation as being typified by office, service-oriented, and commercial uses which provide retail and related goods and services to local-sub-regional and regional markets. Areas designated as Highway Commercial tend to be located in the outlying or newly developed areas of the city. Neighborhood convenience centers shall be located within easy walking distance of residents in the area, and where they will be compatible with the character of the surrounding area. Commercial uses located adjacent to residential uses shall utilize significant buffering and landscaping to minimize negative impacts. Future development will be reviewed to meet the requirements of the LDRs. Additionally, the applicant plans to develop commercial uses to serve the surrounding area. Therefore, the request is compatible with the Comprehensive Plan and the 2050 Vision Plan.
The proposed land use designation, Highway Commercial, is consistent with the surrounding area, and is not expected to create any land use incompatibilities.
In accordance with standard practice from the Florida Department of Economic Opportunity (DEO) and other review agencies, an impact comparison analysis of the proposed amendment has been completed based upon the theoretical maximum development potential under the currently adopted future land use designation versus the proposed designation. The facility analysis presented in the staff report suggests the proposed land use amendment should not cause any of the City’s public infrastructure and services to degrade below the adopted or current operational level of service (LOS) based on the theoretical maximum impact analysis.
At the April 15, 2026, Planning Board meeting, the Board voted 5-0 to recommend approval of the request for a future land use map amendment.

The C-2 zoning district allows for general commercial uses, such as the proposed Ace Hardware; however, outdoor storage and outdoor display is limited to only in the rear of the building. description:
Current city code prohibits riding bicycles, skateboards and the like on the sidewalks generally in the downtown area. The attached ordinance has been updated since first reading to include a specific map and listing of the road segments adjacent to which bikes, etc. cannot be ridden on the sidwalks. The Police Department has also recommended adding "micromobility devices" to the list of conveyances which are prohibited in this location. Additionally, under the current ordinance a violation is a criminal offense (a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of up to $500 and up to 60 days in jail). The Police Department has recommended that the ordinance be revised to make the first offense a non-criminal offense which carries a $250 fine and that subsequent violations by the same person would then be a criminal violation. The Police Department has also suggested that the City Commission consider adopting an ordinance requiring persons under 18 years of age to wear helmets on e-bikes and micromobility devices.
The attached ordinance provides a new definition for "micromobility devices"; adds micromobility devices to the list of prohibited conveyances on sidewalks downtown; Provides that first offenses carry a $250 fine and that subsequent violations by the same person would then be a criminal violation.
In addition, the attached ordinance also requires persons under 18 years of age to wear helmets on bicycles, e-bikes and micromobility devices. The Police Department did not specifically recommend helmets for bicycle riders, but the City Attorney added this for consistency. The City Commission can choose to adopt the new helmet regulations for all three, or apply it to one, two or none. The new provision is included predominantly for discussion purposes, but if the Commission wants to adopt it they are free to do so, or it can be modified or completely removed for second reading.
First reading of this ordinance was held on March 16, 2026.
title: Second reading of Ordinance Amending Sections 28-9, 28-10 and adding a new Section 28-10.1 regarding e-bikes, micromobility devices and bicycle operation on downtown sidewalks and use of helmets by riders 16-17 years of age.

A traffic Impact Analysis or memo will be required at the time of site plan or subdivision. If the development is projected to create more than 1,000 ADT per day, a full traffic study will be required.
Stormwater retention will be designed at the time of site plan or subdivision plat. The stormwater system will be designed to meet all required governmental regulations, and it shall be designed to accommodate a 100-year, 24-hour storm event which will be retained on site.

description:
The applicant, GlassHouse Square, LLC, submitted a rezoning application which was previously denied by the City Commission on first reading of the rezoning ordinance. The applicant appealed the Commission’s decision and the court has entered an order which requires the City to consider the rezoning application anew. The City Commission is conducting a new first reading. The rezoning application is the exact same application that was voted on by the City Commission previously. The Court’s order does not mandate any particular decision. It requires only the City Commission conduct a proper hearing and support its decision, of either approval or denial, on competent substantial evidence and reasons that are germane to the rezoning request.
The applicant, GlassHouse Square, LLC, has submitted an application to rezone the property located at 130 W. New York Avenue from C-2A, Downtown Commercial to GlassHouse Square PD. The site consists of a single structure, the former county jail, and associated parking. The proposed development calls for the existing but long vacant jail building to be demolished, and a phased redevelopment project built in its place. Phase 1 of the proposed development plan is for a two-story retail/commercial and office building with rooftop entertainment space along New York Avenue, 15 temporary off-street parking spaces along Georgia Avenue, a pedestrian walkway on the east side of the property running from Georgia Avenue to New York Avenue, and a gathering space between the building and temporary parking area. Phase 2 calls for a two-story mixed-use building, including 5 residential units, adjacent to Georgia Avenue where the temporary parking is located in Phase 1. The current plan does not have a definitive timeframe for the development of Phase 2 nor a plan for where the required permanent parking spaces would be developed.
The applicant had been made aware from the beginning of this process that they needed to identify sufficient parking for the project. The applicant’s architect has calculated the parking required by city code to be 113 parking spaces (memo attached) and City staff agrees that the architect's calculation is correct. This proposed PD does not provide for the required on-site, code compliant amount of parking, nor does it identify a specific location for off-site parking. The applicant has made various proposals for parking the project which do not provide for the required parking. When this PD was considered on first reading on September 26, 2022, the Commissioners stated that they wanted specifics on the number of spaces and where they would be provided for. That first reading was continued to allow the applicant to revise its proposal vis-à-vis the parking. The applicant’s new proposal was heard at a continuation of the first reading on June 5, 2023, and was ultimately denied. The application that is before the City Commission is the same application that the Commission denied when it considered rezoning on June 5, 2023.
The proposed development agreement for this requested PD rezoning includes the following provisions:
1. A minimum of 50 parking spaces, 40 spaces for Phase 1 and 10 spaces for Phase 2, will be provided either on-site (maximum of 15), offsite to be located within 800' of the site, or through payment of a "parking mitigation fee" in the amount of $10,000 per waived parking space. Unlike ordinary proposals, the requested PD does not identify specific locations or number of spaces, other than the 15 on-site spaces that are in the location where the Phase 2 building would go.
2. A publicly accessible green square that may or may not include a water feature will be constructed in Phase 1.
3. A Pedestrian Walkway will be constructed in Phase 1 that will generally be open to the public between 8:00 a.m. and 12:00 a.m. A draft of the easement agreement that would regulate the Pedestrian Walkway is attached to this agenda item.
4. The project must comply with architectural standards that maintain consistency with the character of the historic downtown area. The Historic Preservation Board approved a conditional Certificate of Appropriateness related to the overall building design at their August 4, 2022 meeting. The Board required that the applicant submit additional information related to proposed building materials at a later date.
5. Allowed uses will be the same as C-2A with a few additions and restrictions.
6. Vibrations will have to be monitored and minimized during all construction activities (demolition of the existing jail building will be completed by the City; steps will be taken to prevent damage to adjacent structures during the demolition process).
With respect to the applicant's request to provide for a payment in lieu of parking, Section 33-91.03(k) provides for the creation of a special parking district by the City Commission where parking or transit facilities may be provided by the city, thus lessening the demand for on-site parking. For development proposed in these districts, the City Commission may allow the developer to pay a fee in lieu of providing some or all of the spaces required by this section. The amount of the fee would be determined by the City Commission and be equal to the land acquisition, construction and maintenance costs of the parking spaces that are deferred. Currently, no special parking districts have been established nor are any in the planning stages.
title: First Reading of Ordinance Changing the Zoning for GlassHouse Square PD, on Approximately 0.868 Acre of Property, Located at 130 West New York Avenue from C-2A to Planned Development.

description:
In 2020, the City purchased and implemented BS&A Software as its Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system. BS&A Software has since announced a transition for all on-premise clients to its cloud-based platform, known as BS&A Online. Moving forward, all software enhancements, feature updates, and system improvements will be available exclusively through the cloud version of the software.
The Fiscal Year 2025/2026 adopted budget includes the necessary funding to support the upgrade and migration to BS&A Online. These funds encompass software implementation costs, staff training, required travel, and project management services associated with the transition.
The proposed resolution authorizes the City to proceed with the upgrade and migration from the on-premise BS&A system to the BS&A Online cloud platform, ensuring continued access to system updates, enhanced functionality, and long-term operational support.
title: Consideration re Contract for Software and Services for BS&A Cloud.

description:
The City Utilities Department applied for a grant that was based on the 2024 Hurricanes of Helen and Milton that caused flooding of several structures at the Wiley M. Nash wastewater and the Lift Station #1 on Wisconsin Avenue. Based on documents that were submitted, the city was recently informed that we would receive a grant in the amount of $7,600,000 with no repayment required to assist with making these two areas more resilient.
To complete the grant award, the project will need to submit additional documents. This project involves providing and submitting a completed SA-HWM CWSRF loan application and resolution approved by the City Commission and signed by the mayor. In addition, a legal opinion must be signed by the City Attorney and EPA 4700 and FFATA documents by the City Manager. The above items must be completed, signed, and returned as soon as possible to meet the March deadline.
As previously mentioned, this project will improve the elevation adjustment of the Wiley M. Nash Advance Wastewater Facility west headworks, generator and main electrical switchgear replacement and bar screen areas that were not upgraded with the ongoing improvements, and lift station #1 relocation. Only lift station #1 is currently designed and ready to bid. The rest of the projects will need to be assigned as a future budget amendment and task assignment.
title: Resolution Approving SA-HMW CW SRF Loan Application.

description:
The ± 143.8-acre subject property known as the DeLand Tech Park PD, was originally approved on October 3, 2022, and is within the Southwest Activity Center. The purpose of this amendment is to modify the existing PD to add one additional use to the list of commercial uses permitted within the development.
Currently, the Tech Park PD agreement allows for a variety of commercial and industrial uses, including packaged sales of beer and/or wine (package sales where beer and/or wine are sold for consumption off-premises with a DBPR 2APS license), as well as restaurants serving beer, wine and liquor, for on-site consumption. This amendment clarifies that in addition to restaurant sales, packaged beer, wine and liquor, such as those offered by a liquor/package store or similar retail establishment (uses requiring a DBPR 3PS liquor license (package sales) would be allowed within the PD. Any establishment that intends on selling alcohol will be required to obtain a proper state license from the Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation (DBPR).
Besides the additional use, there are no proposed changes to the DeLand Tech Park PD agreement and the developer will need to follow the requirements that were previously outlined in the agreement.
On November 12, 2025, the Planning Board unanimously voted to recommend approval of the PD amendment.
On December 15, 2025, the City Commission unanimously voted to approve the PD amendment on First Reading.
On January 5, 2025, the City Commission continued Second Reading to accommodate a procedural issue.
title: Second Reading of Ordinance No. 2026-03, Approving a Second Amendment to the DeLand Tech Park PD to Allow for One Additional Use, for Property, Located on the South Side of Cassadaga Road, West of Interstate 4.

description:
In the 24/25 fiscal budget, the Utilities Department received approval by the adoption of the budget for the personnel and equipment to implemented a fats, oil and grease (FOG) management program to align with Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP) and the State of Florida Administrative Code (F.A.C.) 62-705 concerning grease waste removal and disposal. The purpose of this City program is to proactively monitor the largest grease producing commercial establishments in the city, bringing them into compliance and reduce the environmental risks that occur with sanitary sewer overflows caused by fats, oils and grease discharge.
The (FDEP) issued Domestic Wastewater Facility Permit for the Wiley M. Nash Water Reclamation Facility, under F.A.C. 62-705, also requires that the City adopt regulations which prohibit illicit discharge to the City’s wastewater collection’s system from commercial establishments providing for control of fats, oil and grease pollutant contributions to the City’s wastewater collection’s systems and the point of treatment. The attached ordinance is intended to fulfill these permit requirements.
In accordance with instructions from the City Commission at the first reading of this Ordinance, the City Attorney has removed the requirement to charge a fee for permit issuance or routine inspections.
title: Second Reading of Ordinance No. 2026-04, Amending Chapter 30, Section 30-3, and Adding Section 30-49A, Oil and Grease Management Program.

description:
The applicant, Longleaf Four, LLC, is requesting approval of a preliminary plat for the DeLand Tech Park PD. The applicant seeks to subdivide the subject property into three developable lots, along with tracts for stormwater ponds, tree protection areas, landscape buffers, and other site infrastructure. As described in the original Planned Development, the applicant seeks to develop the eastern side of the subject property as industrial space and the western side of the property as commercial/neighborhood retail. This is the first of three phases of development for the DeLand Tech Park PD.
Phase I (current preliminary plat) includes the construction of Kirk and Ulysses Drive (formerly to-be-known as Pinehurst Drive) to provide site access and transportation circulation, associated infrastructure improvements, and mass clearing and grading of the property. Ulysses Drive will connect to Martin Luther King Jr. Beltway to the west of the property, and Kirk Drive will connect Cassadaga Road to SR 472. The preliminary plat had shown this right of way in tracts. However, the plan has been revised to relabel the right of way. Both roads are being dedicated to the city. The right-of-way will include landscaping, a pedestrian/bicycle trail, three stormwater ponds, and other associated infrastructure.
The ponds are part of a master stormwater system that is designed to retain the 100-year/24-hour storm event for the entire site at full buildout, which includes up to 70% impervious area for the eastern Industrial area and up to 60% impervious area for the western Retail area set forth by the DeLand Tech Park PD.
The applicant intends to mass grade the entire site and install infrastructure, roadways, and stormwater ponds for the entire development. However, since individual sites and lots will be developed in multiple phases, over many years, staff is including a condition of approval to address the need for site stabilization to help mitigate off-site impacts. The following conditions have been added to the preliminary plat approval:
On December 10, 2025, the Planning Board unanimously voted to approve the preliminary plat, with the following conditions:
1. The applicant shall revise the preliminary plat to show all public roadway as right-of-way, rather than tracts. The tract tables and site data tables shall also be revised to reflect the right of way designation.
2. To minimize stormwater impacts and ensure the site is stabilized for the duration of the development, all areas disturbed by construction, and soil stockpiles, shall be stabilized as soon as possible to reduce the duration of soil exposure to runoff events and the potential for erosion. All stockpiles shall be encompassed by silt fence. All disturbed areas which are either final graded, or will remain inactive for a period of more than 7 days, shall be required to be stabilized within 7 days of the completion of the grading activities. Stabilization may include, but not be limited to seeding, hydromulching and/or resodding.
The applicant has since submitted a revised preliminary plat and construction plans, showing the roads as right of way instead of tracts, therefore, satisfying the first condition. The second condition will remain.
title: Resolution Approving Preliminary Plat, DeLand Tech Park, Located at 1445 Cassadaga Road.

description:
The City of DeLand currently operates one hundred and forty-seven (147) sewage lift stations throughout the DeLand Utility Service Area. Approximately four additional stations are dedicated to the city by developers each year. Due to the need to standardize equipment for maintenance purposes, the city has accepted only Smith & Loveless sewage lift stations from developers and uses this equipment exclusively to replace existing lift stations which are no longer in good working order after twenty-five years or need to be up-sized.
For many years, the city has purchased replacement pump stations using a purchase agreement with Smith & Loveless Inc., the most recent of which will expire on December 31, 2025. This relationship has been beneficial to the City in terms of favorable pricing and ability to quickly procure these stations. The city was able to expedite replacement of stations that were damaged by the hurricanes and subsequent tornadoes, cutting the delivery time to a shorter period.
This purchase agreement will be the sixth executed five-year contract between the City and Smith & Loveless Inc. Staff this year negotiated with the local representative, Hydra Services, Inc., and the Smith & Loveless main headquarters, resulting in the subject proposal. The proposed purchase agreement provides a menu of prices for various size lift stations which can be used to purchase this equipment for a period of five years. Purchase prices are good through December 31, 2030. Staff would also like to point out that allowing this annual fixed rate multiplier increase over the term of the contract will help us avoid a larger increase at the end of contract for the next five years if we wish to continue this arrangement in the future. This rate remains the same as what the city has used for purchases over the last ten years and is favorable to the city.
title: Resolution Approving Sole Source Purchase Agreement for Sewage Pumping Stations.

description:
As the City Commission is aware, the EPA has established limits on emerging contaminants of Perfluorooctanesulfonic Acid and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (also known collectively as PFAS) in public water supply systems. Utilities staff have been testing the water supply wells and water plants to determine the extent of these contaminants per EPA limits. Only six currently have a legal Maximum Contaminant Level (MCL) limit at this time set on different chemicals in our water supply system. Current PFAS regulations will require the City to achieve compliance by April 26, 2029. However, the EPA in early 2026 has posted on their website that it is their intention to consider moving that date out to 2031.
The Utilities department has determined that at a minimum, six of the water plants will need some sort of upgrade to assist with this removal requirement. This task order was requested to perform a preliminary design and determine the best recommended treatment process at those sites and to prepare a facility plan that would be required for an FDEP drinking water State Revolving Fund (SRF) loan and possible grant forgiveness. The facility plan will help to provide a cost estimate for land purchases, plant modifications required, and construction.
title: Consideration re Facilities Work Plan and Funding Assistance for Professional Services Task Order Proposal for Perfluorooctanesulfonic Acid and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) Removal

description:
The City Commission previously adopted Resolution Number 2024-31 which prohibits videotaping in the Police Department lobby. The Police Department has requested that this policy be made a part of the City's Code of Ordinances. By way of background, the lobby of the DeLand Police Department is open to the public and, like many police departments, it is equipped with a bullet-proof window behind which a uniformed or civilian employee works for the purpose of interacting with citizens who need to, or at least believe that they may need to, engage with law enforcement for various purposes including but not limited to reporting crimes, seeking or providing information and accessing resources. People have begun videotaping citizens speaking to law enforcement personnel while in the lobby, and in many cases broadcasting the recordings on the internet or through social media pages. The Police Department lobby is, of course, open to the public but the citizens making initial contact with Police Department staff in the lobby are sharing potentially sensitive information and have some expectation of privacy in this area.
On December 1, 2025, the City Commission adopted this Ordinance on First Reading.
title: Second Reading of Ordinance No.2026-01, Codifying the City's Existing Videotaping Policy into the Code of Ordinances.

description:
On June 20, 2025, Senate Bill 784 was signed into law with an effective date of July 1, 2025. The law prohibits local governments from submitting subdivision plats and replats which are made for recording (i.e. final plats) to their governing bodies for review. The law does allow the City to submit preliminary plats to its Planning Board and City Commission for review. The law also requires municipalities to designate an administrative authority to receive, review, and process plat and replat submittals, and an administrative official responsible for approving, approving with conditions, or denying proposed plats and replats. In response to SB 784, staff in conjunction with the City Attorney are proposing to designate the City’s Planning Department as the administrative authority to receive, review, and process plat and replat submittals, and the Planning Director as the administrative official to approve, approve with condition or deny proposed plats and replats for recording. SB 784 does allow preliminary plats to go before Planning Board and City Commission for review and since preliminary plats do not involve policy considerations and are primarily a technical review, staff is proposing that preliminary plats and construction plans go before Planning Board for final consideration. Other proposed changes are to simplify the process by eliminating the requirement of a sketch plan and clearly outlining required items for preliminary plats, construction plans, and final plats.
On December 15, 2025, the City Commission unanimously voted to approve the proposed ordinance on First Reading..
title: Second Reading of Ordinance No. 2026-02, Amending Chapter 33, Land Development Regulations Related To Subdivision Plat Approval.

description:

This project picks up where phase 6 left off, and includes the installation of approximately 1,200 LF of reuse transmission main and 5,500 LF of distribution mains to serve Phase #1 of the Mallory Square Subdivision and connect the River Chase Subdivision. description:
The Utilities Department owns, operates, and maintains two elevated storage tanks in the current water distribution system. An agreement to maintain them was signed with Utility Service Co., Inc in 2008 for the tanks to be inspected, cleaned, repaired, painted and yearly Engineer certified stamped report provided.
The city received good service during the first twelve years of the agreement. Since that time, they have changed management ownership several times and each time the service has declined slightly. The inspections are not done in a timely manner, inspection reports are sent uncertified, Water Plant #2 elevated tank several times has had pieces fall off the tank and they were slow to respond and to repair. This being our tank that is over a hundred years old has given us great concern.
This past summer we asked two other companies to come on site and evaluate the tanks and give us an opinion. They both felt the tanks were structurally sound but could use additional attention to get them back in a well maintained condition, which was expected. Photos of WP#2 tank top and hand rail gave us great concern and we feel that Utility Service Co., Inc. has gotten complacent and we need to move onto a different vendor.

description:
The subject property is located directly south of the West Volusia Shopping Center, across from Firehouse Rd. It was previously rezoned from C-2, General Commercial, to the Mainstreet Townhomes Planned Development (PD) on August 7, 2006. The Mainstreet Townhomes PD approved 66 multi-family townhome units, but the project was abandoned after the rezoning was approved.
The C-2 zoning district allows for a range of commercial uses such as office/medical uses, personal service uses, hospitality uses as well as vehicular service uses and multi-family uses. The C-2 zoned district differs from the Mainstreet Townhomes PD which only allows multi-family townhomes as a permitted use.
On June 11, 2025, the Planning Board voted 3-1 to recommend denial of the rezone request. At the meeting, both citizens and Board members voiced concern over the uncertainty of future development and impacts upon the neighboring Wellington Woods residential subdivision located directly to the east of the subject property.
On July 21, 2025, the City Commission voted to continue the request to the August 18, 2025, City Commission meeting.
On August 18, 2025, the City Commission voted to continue the request to the October 6, 2025, City Commission meeting.
On October 6, 2025, the City Commission voted to continue the request to the November 17, 2025, City Commission meeting, allowing the applicant more time to meet with nearby residents of Wellington Woods and their concerns.
On October 24, 2025, a neighborhood meeting was held and attended by the applicant, Jessica Gow of CobbCole, the owners of the subject property and 8 adjacent residents from Wellington Woods. The topics discussed included:
Distance from Carwash building to rear property line (645 ft., about an 8th of a mile) and sound buffering, which should not be an issue with that distance.
Distance from the homeowners' property line to future potential development in the rear of the property – the discussion centered around the Property Owner and residents agreeing that the potential for retail development in that corridor was highly unlikely based on site layout, and the residents requested, and the owner agreed, that the owner will work with the City to install opaque fencing along that boundary when/if development in the rear moves forward – inside of the 25’ setback/natural preservation area proposed.
Residents agreed there is no need for a written use restriction based on the practical constraints of the site and limitations on uses in the rear.
Residents and Property Owner agreed that based on the info discussed, they would no longer oppose the zoning request with the assurance there would be a fence in the area discussed.
On November 17, 2025, the City Commission voted 4-1 to approve the rezone request, on first reading.
title: Second Reading of Ordinance No. 2025-27, Changing the Zoning for Approximately 7.35 Acres of Property, Located on South Woodland Boulevard from Mainstreet Townhomes PD to C-2 (General Commercial). First Reading 11-17-25.

description:
The ± 143.8-acre subject property known as the DeLand Tech Park PD, was originally approved on October 3, 2022, and is within the Southwest Activity Center. The purpose of this amendment is to modify the existing PD to add one additional use to the list of commercial uses permitted within the development.
Currently, the Tech Park PD agreement allows for a variety of commercial and industrial uses, including packaged sales of beer and/or wine (package sales where beer and/or wine are sold for consumption off-premises with a DBPR 2APS license), as well as restaurants serving beer, wine and liquor, for on-site consumption. This amendment clarifies that in addition to restaurant sales, packaged beer, wine and liquor, such as those offered by a liquor/package store or similar retail establishment (uses requiring a DBPR 3PS liquor license (package sales)) would be allowed within the PD. Any establishment that intends on selling alcohol will be required to obtain a proper state license from the Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation (DBPR).
Besides the additional use, there are no proposed changes to the DeLand Tech Park PD agreement and the developer will need to follow the requirements that were previously outlined in the agreement.
On November 12, 2025, the Planning Board unanimously voted to recommend approval of the PD amendment.
title: First Reading of Ordinance Approving a Second Amendment to the DeLand Tech Park PD to Allow for One Additional Use, for Property Located on the South Side of Cassadaga Road, West of Interstate 4.

description: On June 20, 2025, Senate Bill 784 was signed into law with an effective date of July 1, 2025. The law prohibits local governments from submitting subdivision plats and replats which are made for recording (i.e. final plats) to their governing bodies for review. The law does allow the City to submit preliminary plats to its Planning Board and City Commission for review. The law also requires municipalities to designate an administrative authority to receive, review, and process plat and replat submittals, and an administrative official responsible for approving, approving with conditions, or denying proposed plats and replats. In response to SB 784, staff in conjunction with the City Attorney are proposing to designate the City’s Planning Department as the administrative authority to receive, review, and process plat and replat submittals, and the Planning Director as the administrative official to approve, approve with condition or deny proposed plats and replats for recording. SB 784 does allow preliminary plats to go before Planning Board and City Commission for review and since preliminary plats do not involve policy considerations and are primarily a technical review, staff is proposing that preliminary plats and construction plans go before Planning Board for final consideration. Other proposed changes are to simplify the process by eliminating the requirement of a sketch plan and clearly outlining required items for preliminary plats, construction plans, and final plats.
title: First Reading of Ordinance Amending Chapter 33, Land Development Regulations Related To Subdivision Plat Approval.

description:
Victoria Park Community Council Inc. is requesting approval to remove one (1) historic tree located in the Common Area along Martin Luther King Beltway. The Land Development Regulations require that, before the removal of any historic trees should occur, it must be approved by the City Commission. Section 33-57.05(d) states that there must be a finding that the tree is a hazard (due to health or natural damage) or that it is not economically or practically feasible to develop the parcel without removing the tree. The City Forester has determined that the tree proposed for removal is a 28” DBH historic Live Oak that was likely struck by lightning, and it has died due to natural causes. The applicant, Victoria Park Community Council Inc., is requesting the removal because the tree is a hazard due to its condition.
At the November 18th Tree Advisory Committee meeting, the Arborist Inspector’s PowerPoint was presented demonstrating the tree proposed for removal is a 28” DBH historic Live Oak that appears dead, and that it was most likely struck by lightning. The applicant is requesting the removal of the tree because the tree is a hazard due to its condition. Because of the tree’s deteriorated condition, by a unanimous vote, the Tree Advisory Committee recommended approval of the removal of the 28” Live Oak tree with a replacement requirement of one (1) six- (6-) inch caliper Live Oak to be planted on the property adjacent to the location of the dead tree. It was the opinion of the Tree Advisory Committee members voting to approve the removal that reduced replacement would be appropriate to help restore the lost canopy without unnecessarily burdening the Homeowners Association by requiring 100 percent DBH replacement.
title: Resolution Approving the Removal of One (1) Historic Tree, Located in Victoria Hills Common Area along Martin Luther King Beltway.
