description:
The City’s contract with Avcon for airport consulting services was approved by the Commission on February 17, 2020. The term of the Agreement was for three years with two, one-year terms by mutual agreement of the parties. Both FAA and FDOT require that consultants should be selected via a competitive negotiation process no later than every five years.
Staff is in the process of developing a new Request for Expressions of Interest and Statements of Qualifications (RFQ) for airport consultants and intends to advertise shortly. According to State requirements for consultant selection, the expressions of interest, when received, would need to be reviewed and ranked by a selection committee, interviews of a short list of firms conducted if deemed necessary, and a final ranking recommended to and approved by the Commission prior to beginning negotiation of a new contract and fees with the top ranked firm.
In the past, the City Commission has expressed its desire to appoint a member of its board to serve on the selection committee with members of the city staff. The purpose of this RCA is to request this Commission appointment. ​
title: Consideration re Appointment of City Commission Member to Airport Consultant Selection Committee.

description:
The City of DeLand Vulnerability Assessment & Adaptation Plan grant was selected for funding by Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP) on December 18, 2023. FDEP Standard Grant Agreement was approved by the City Commission on May 20, 2024.
The Vulnerability Assessment is evaluating the vulnerabilities of critical and regionally significant assets to a broad range of flood hazards and will subsequently prioritize flood and climate adaptation action items which can be pursued through grant funding, local policies, and the identification of implementation activities. Since the City of DeLand is an inland community with limited vulnerabilities caused by tidal influences, the objective of the assessment will be to evaluate flood hazard vulnerabilities caused by current and future rainfall, stormwater runoff, hurricanes, and compound flooding. The FDEP Grant provides 100% funding for the City of DeLand Vulnerability Assessment & Adaptation Plan.
This Change Order No. 1 will provide City Consultant, Halff, with additional time to complete required tasks by FDEP. In addition, there are updates to the Special Terms and Conditions, Performance Measures and Consequences for Non-performance, and Attachment 6 following updates from the Office of the General Counsel and Resilient Florida Program. ​
title: Consideration re City of DeLand Vulnerability Assessment & Adaptation Plan, Change Order No. 1 to FDEP Standard Grant Agreement.

description:
In 2022 the City Commission considered a resolution (numbered 2022-72) for the adoption of the Beresford Reserve Brownfield Advisory Committee. The Commission at that time voted to approve the resolution with a change to provide for a termination date. At that point in time, it was believed that the remediation planning process would have progressed much more quickly with State of Florida and that the resolution would be ​brought back with a termination date at the same time that ​the ​Committee members were appointed. However, it has taken much longer for the remediation planning process ​than originally anticipated, but the City is now ready to appoint the members to the Committee. As such, the original resolution is being brought back with a few changes, to include a specific termination ​provision and the appointment of five specific members, who are identified below. In addition, a ​few ​changes were made to the ​original resolution for the purpose of giving more guidance to the members for conducting their meetings and ​addressing the frequency of meetings.
The Brownfield Advisory Committee requires the appointment of five (5) members for the Beresford Reserve project. The following individuals have submitted applications for consideration:
Joseph DeGaetano
Denise DeGarmo
Brian Diaz
Catherine Clark
Lance Harding
CRITERIA:
Each Brownfield Advisory Committee shall consist of an odd number of members numbering no less than three and no more than seven, each of whom shall be appointed by the City Commission to serve for the duration of the Committee, unless a different term shall be set by the City Commission. The City Commission may appoint or remove members of the Committee at any time. The members may or may not be City residents, but should have a relation to the area in which the Committee has jurisdiction such as a resident, business owner, property owner, and the City Commission should strive to appoint one or more members with training or expertise in the fields of environmental science and economic development. The City Manager or his designee shall serve as an ex officio member of the Committee who shall not have a vote, but may be elected to be a presiding officer and shall serve as a City Commission liaison to the Committee.
Staff has contacted the applicants and advised them of the City Commission meeting date.
title: Consideration re Beresford Reserve Brownfield Advisory Committee Appointments and Resolution Creating the Beresford Reserve Brownfield Advisory Committee .

description:
The applicant is requesting to amend the Planned Development Agreement for the DeLand Tech Park Planned Development, which was approved by the City Commission on October 3, 2022, originally consisting of 140.07 acres. The purpose of the amendment is to incorporate additional 3.73 acres of property into the existing Planned Development, update the expiration date of the Planned Development and to allow for off-site Tree Protection Area (TPA).
The amendment provides the option to utilize adjacent property for off-site Tree Protection Area through an easement dedicated to the City of DeLand. The easement agreement will ensure that the city has access to inspect the property. However, all maintenance will be the responsibility of the owner/owner’s association. Additionally, the amended agreement requires that when the city determines that it is legally permissible to annex an offsite TPA into the DeLand Tech Park PD, the applicant shall submit an application to once again amend the PD agreement to formally include the offsite TPA within twelve (12) months from the date notice is provided to the city. At that point, once annexed into the city, the offsite TPA will be incorporated into the DeLand Tech Park PD, via an amendment to the PD agreement.
Since first reading, additional edits were made to the amended PD agreement. The changes address internal landscaping requirements, building setbacks and building orientation. Exposed, insulated metal panels are proposed if part of a cold storage or refrigerated storage facility or structure. An example elevation is attached to this amendment. All changes since first reading are in the amended PD agreement and are highlighted in yellow.
On August 14, 2024, the Planning Board recommended approval of the zoning amendment.
On August 19, 2024, the City Commission unanimously voted to approve the zoning amendment on first reading.
On October 21, 2024, the City Commission voted to continue the item to the meeting on November 4, 2024, per the applicant's request.
On November 4, 2024, the City Commission voted to continue the item to the meeting on December 16, 2024, per the applicant's request.
On December 16, 2024, the City Commission voted to continue the item to the meeting on January 6, 2024, per the applicant's request.
This is a request to continue the item to the January 21, 2025, City Commission meeting.
title: Request to Continue the Second Reading of Ordinance No. 2024-43, Amending the DeLand Tech Park PD, for 143.80 Acres of Property Located on the South Side of Cassadaga Road, West of Interstate 4.

description:
The Volusia Legislative Delegation will hold their annual Delegation hearings on January 7th 2025. During this hearing, the City of DeLand presents a legislative program consisting of issues of concern and requests for action or assistance. This program also includes several of the priority items identified by the Florida League of Cities because of their impact on all Florida cities.
The following legislative initiatives are what City staff proposed to include in this year's City program:Enterprise Fund Transfers
Affordable Housing
Property Taxes
Sovereign Immunity
One Water
Annexation
Impact Fees
Local Business Taxes
Public Safety Recruitment and Retention
Electric Vehicles
In addition to the legislative priorities listed above, the City will be seeking an appropriation request for The Bridge.
Staff recommends that the City support the legislative platform document and its accompanying Resolution.
If there are any additional legislative program requests from the City Commission tonight, staff will also incorporate those into the final City legislative program. After tonight, staff and the City's Lobbyist will work to finalize the formal City program so that we will have it to distribute when needed.
title: Resolution Approving Florida League of Cities Legislative Platform and City of DeLand Legislative Program 2025.

description: In a referendum held August 20, 2024, the voters of the City of DeLand approved an Ad Valorem Tax Abatement program for qualified new or expanding businesses. This referendum enabled the city to continue offering the Tax Abatement Program that was originally approved in 1995, and subsequently reapproved in 2005 and 2015. The proposed guidelines do not include a specific wage scale and reference that the maximum allowable abatement shall be based upon compliance with the applicable employment/sales criteria outlined in F.S. 196.012 and the State of Florida Average Annual County Wage Data in effect at the time of Commission action on a request for tax abatement consideration.
title: Resolution Approving the Establishment of Ad Valorem Tax Abatement Guidelines.
